_readme: Grammar structures in the Kannada course, read by tools/grammar-check.mjs.
Same format as structures/telugu.json. For each one:
introducedIn  the lesson that TEACHES it (vocab teach screen or a grammarNote that explains it).
null = the course uses it but never teaches it.
basis         the curriculum text the tag rests on, so you can check it without opening curriculum.js.
confidence    'sure' = quoted from a grammarNote / vocab teach line; 'guess' = my reading.
Every 'guess' NEEDS A FLUENT KANNADA SPEAKER to confirm. The tagger was not one, and
Farhaan (Telugu speaker, learning Kannada) cannot confirm them either.
detect        regexes run over each drill answer (lowercased, punctuation stripped, whole words).
A drill REQUIRES a structure only if its correct answer AND every acceptable form match;
if some accepted form avoids it, the drill merely EXPOSES it.
Empty detect = not auto-detectable, so only (2) "too many at once" sees it.
except        whole tokens that match detect but are not this structure (lexical items).
Derived only from the Kannada curriculum (phrases, conversations, grammarNotes, vocab teach lines).
Lesson pool drills are not checked, matching the Telugu run. Edit freely; nothing else reads this file.

structures.name: -ene / -eeni / -ini verb ending = 'I'
structures.basis: L1 P1 grammarNote: 'The -eeni at the end already means "I", so you don't need naanu.' L3 vocab Hoguttene: 'The -ttene at the end already means "I"'. L11 vocab Iddene and L22 vocab Baruttade ('-ene is "I", -ade is "it"') repeat it. The course accepts -eeni/-ini/-ene as the same ending (colloquial vs written).

structures.name: -eera ending = polite 'you'
structures.basis: L1 P1 grammarNote: 'Change it to -eera, as in iddeera, and it means "you".' L1 P2: 'the -eera at the end already means "you"'. Only ever drilled inside hegiddeera.

structures.name: 'X is Y' with no verb
structures.example: Idu pustaka; Ivaru nanna snehita; Naanu illi
structures.basis: L2 P2 grammarNote: 'There's no word for "is" here, and none is needed. Kannada just puts the two words side by side.' L3 C3 note extends it to 'naanu illi'.

structures.name: question word at the end, after the thing asked about
structures.example: Idu yenu? Mane yelli? Ivaru yaaru?
structures.basis: L2 P1 grammarNote: 'In Kannada, question words usually go at the end.' L1 already drills hegiddeera as a chunk. L15 C1 note: yaake is the exception that often comes first.

structures.name: i- = near, a- = far (idu/adu, illi/alli, ivaru/avaru)
structures.basis: L2 vocab Adu: 'Idu is near, adu is far. Only the first sound changes.' L3 vocab Illi/Alli and L6 vocab Avaru restate the pattern.

structures.name: -ge = 'to' (direction), also 'at' a time
structures.basis: L3 vocab Mane: 'To say "to the house", add -ge to the end: manege.' L12 C3 grammarNote: 'Add -ge to gante for "at"... the same -ge as in manege.' L28 C2: 'Oorige works like manege'.

structures.name: ide = 'it is / there is' (things, places)
structures.example: Mane alli ide; chennagide; kelasa ide
structures.basis: L3 vocab Ide: '"it is" or "there is", for things... For yourself, leave it out'. L9 vocab Chennagide: 'chennagi + ide'.

structures.name: -uttene = 'I go / I will go' (non-past)
structures.basis: L3 vocab Hoguttene: '"I go" or "I will go"... also covers "I'm going"'. L14 vocab Maaduttene re-teaches it as the future: 'drop the -idd- and you get "I will do"'. Tagged at L3, where it first appears with its meaning.

structures.name: bare verb = blunt command ('Go!')
structures.basis: L3 vocab 'Hogu = Go... telling someone to go'. That this bare form is the blunt one is only implied at L10 ('hogu ("go!") becomes the polite hogi'). NEEDS A FLUENT KANNADA SPEAKER: is bare hogu actually rude/informal in the way the course implies?

structures.name: object + beku/beda, no subject ('water is wanted')
structures.basis: L4 P1 grammarNote: 'Two words, no "I". Neeru beku means "water is wanted"'. L4 P2: 'Use beda instead of beku, not with it'.

structures.name: illa = 'no / not', also fused onto a word (gottilla)
structures.example: Illa, oota beda; ishta illa; gottilla
structures.basis: L4 vocab 'Illa = No / not' and C2 note 'Illa is a general "no" or "not"'. L15 C3 note: 'Illa after ishta makes it "don't like"'. L20 vocab Gottilla: 'gottu + illa, joined into one word'.

structures.name: nanna/nimma/avara/aatana before the noun, noun unchanged
structures.basis: L5 P1 grammarNote: '"My" comes first, then the thing, and nothing changes... Just like English.'

structures.name: respectful he/she: avara, ivaru, avaru (also plural)
structures.basis: L5 vocab Avara: '"his" or "her", said with respect'. L6 vocab Ivaru: 'how you say "he" or "she" about someone right here'. L17 C4 note: 'Ivaru also covers two or more people'.

structures.name: after a number the noun stays singular
structures.basis: L7 P2 grammarNote: 'After a number, the word doesn't change... The number already says there's more than one.' L8 C4 note contrasts eradu pustaka / nanna pustakagalu.

structures.name: -galu = plural of things
structures.basis: L8 vocab Pustakagalu: 'Add -galu to the end of a thing to mean more than one.'

structures.name: -aru = plural of people
structures.basis: L8 vocab Snehitaru: 'For people, add -aru. For things, add -galu.' Only one word ever takes it.

structures.name: adjective before the noun, unchanged
structures.example: dodda mane, olleya oota, kappu batte
structures.basis: L9 P1 grammarNote: 'Dodda ("big") goes before the thing and never changes.' L19 vocab Kappu: 'They go before the thing, like dodda'.

structures.name: 'X IS good' needs chennagide, not olleya
structures.basis: L9 C1 grammarNote: 'Before a thing, use olleya... To say "the food IS good", use chennagide.'

structures.name: -du on an adjective to end a sentence ('my house is small')
structures.basis: L9 C4 grammarNote: 'To end a sentence with it, add -du: nanna mane chikkadu... Same for doddadu and olleyadu.' Mentioned once in a note, never drilled.

structures.name: -i = polite request ('please ...')
structures.basis: L10 P2 grammarNote: 'The -i at the end of kodi makes it polite... hogu becomes the polite hogi'. L16 vocab Heli: 'Same polite -i as kodi.' L3 P2 already accepts 'alli hogi' unexplained. hogi before baru- is excluded (that is the L14 'having gone' form).

structures.name: iddene = 'I am' (for a person's location)
structures.basis: L11 vocab Iddene: '"I am": naanu illi iddene'. L3 C3 note said the opposite way first ('For yourself, just naanu illi') but accepted 'naanu illi iddeeni'.

structures.name: -utt-idd-ene = 'I am doing (right now)'
structures.basis: L11 vocab Hoguttiddene: 'The extra -idd- makes it right now.' L14 vocab Maaduttene: 'drop the -idd-'.

structures.name: the action word goes last (SOV)
structures.basis: L11 P1 grammarNote: 'The action word goes last'. L12 P2: 'the action word always comes last'. Already true of every drill from L3 (manege hoguttene) and L4 (neeru beku); placing it at L11 because that is where it is said. NEEDS A FLUENT KANNADA SPEAKER only to agree it counts as one structure.

structures.name: noun + maadu ('do') for activities: a meal, a bath, sleep, help
structures.example: oota maadu, snaana maadide, sahaaya maaduttene
structures.basis: L11 P3 grammarNote: 'For a meal, Kannada says "do": oota maadu.' L18 vocab Snaana/Nidde and L22 vocab Sahaaya repeat it.

structures.name: past tense, -e = 'I' (did, went, came)
structures.basis: L13 vocab Maadide: 'In the past, the "I" ending is just -e.' L13 vocab Hode: 'The start changes in ways you can't predict... Learn each one.'

structures.name: verb-i before another verb = 'having gone' (hogi baruttene)
structures.basis: L14 C3 grammarNote: 'Put before another action word, hogi means "having gone"'. Only this one fixed goodbye.

structures.name: nanage/nimage ('to me/you') as the subject of like/want/fear/know
structures.example: Nanage idu ishta; Nimage yenu beku?
structures.basis: L15 vocab Nanage: 'For liking and wanting, Kannada says "to me"... never naanu ishta.' L4 P1 note first mentions 'nanage neeru beku'. L16/L20/L22/L26 notes extend it to happy, know, can, feelings.

structures.name: adakke = 'that's why', reason first
structures.basis: L15 vocab Adakke: 'Yaake? asks why; adakke answers it.' L24 vocab Yaakendare contrasts it: 'Adakke works the other way: reason first.'

structures.name: chennagi = 'well', before the verb (vs chennagide 'is good')
structures.basis: L16 vocab Chennagi: 'chennagi says how you did something; chennagide says a thing is good.' C3 note: 'Chennagi sits right before the action.'

structures.name: mattu = 'and' between two nouns
structures.basis: L17 vocab Mattu: 'joins two names or things'.

structures.name: nanage + thing + ide = 'I have' (things going on)
structures.basis: L18 C1 grammarNote: 'To say "I have", Kannada says "to me, it is there": nanage + thing + ide.' L27 P3 contrasts it with nanna hattira.

structures.name: -ittu = 'was' (it was)
structures.basis: L20 vocab Chennagittu: 'The ending -ittu turns "is" into "was".' Only on one word.

structures.name: place words go AFTER the noun (mele, kelage, olage, hattira, jote)
structures.example: meju mele, mane olage, nanna jote
structures.basis: L21 P1 grammarNote: 'These words go AFTER the thing: meju mele, "table on". The opposite of English.'

structures.name: -ina / -a = 'of' before a place word (mejina, maneya)
structures.basis: L21 vocab Meju: 'You'll also hear it as mejina, "of the table"'. Maneya is only in accepted forms, never glossed. The course SHOWS a genitive but never states it as an ending. NEEDS A FLUENT KANNADA SPEAKER: is -ina/-a the right reading, and which nouns take which?

structures.name: -ade = 'it' verb ending (vs -ene 'I')
structures.basis: L22 vocab Baruttade: 'The ending tells you who: -ene is "I", -ade is "it".'

structures.name: nanage + X + baruttade/aaguttade = 'I can' (skill / manage), -uvudilla = can't
structures.basis: L22 vocab Baruttade ('literally "Kannada comes to me"'), Aaguttade ('for time and plans, not skills') and their negatives.

structures.name: verb-a + beku = 'must'
structures.basis: L23 vocab Hogabeku: 'Add beku to an action and it means "must"'. P3 note: 'beku doesn't change for "I" or "you"'. How hogu becomes hoga- is never said.

structures.name: verb-a + baaradu = 'must not'
structures.basis: L23 vocab Maadabaaradu: 'Swap beku for baaradu to forbid'.

structures.name: joining clauses: aadare (but), athava (or), yaakendare (because)
structures.basis: L24 vocab Aadare/Athava/Yaakendare and P2 note: 'Aadare sits between the two halves'.

structures.name: kooda = 'too', right after the person it is about
structures.basis: L24 vocab Kooda: 'It goes right after the person'. C2 note: 'Kooda follows whoever it's about'.

structures.name: past stem + -are = 'if' (hodare, bandare, iddare)
structures.basis: L25 vocab Hodare: 'Take hode, "I went", and swap the -e for -are'. P1 note: 'The "if" is the ending, so it comes last'. Haagaadare ('in that case') is excluded as a fixed word, though it is built the same way.

structures.name: nanage + feeling + aagide/aagilla = 'I feel / don't feel'
structures.basis: L26 vocab Aagide: 'Put it after a feeling: nanage hasivu aagide'. P3 note: 'aagide says yes, aagilla says no'. L29 C2 reuses aagide with sakkath.

structures.name: nanna/nimma hattira = 'I have / you have' (things carried)
structures.basis: L27 P3 grammarNote: 'Nanna hattira, "near me", is for things you carry... Nanage ... ide is for things you have going on'.

structures.name: -a / -ya on the end = yes/no question (ideya, hauda)
structures.basis: L27 vocab Ideya: 'Add -ya to ide and it asks'. L29 vocab Hauda: 'Haudu is "yes". Ask it back, hauda'. Two words only; never generalised to verbs. NEEDS A FLUENT KANNADA SPEAKER: is this one productive ending, as tagged, or two fixed words?

structures.name: -uttide = 'it is ...ing' right now
structures.basis: L28 vocab Baruttide: '"it is coming", right now'. P1 note contrasts baruttene / baruttade / baruttide.

structures.name: alva at the end = '..., right?'
structures.basis: L29 vocab Alva: 'Put alva on the end of anything'.
